response: As I sit here on my 30th birthday, I'm reminded of the countless solitary dinners I've shared with my parents, the only child in a family of three. (In these moments, I've come to realize that I've had to develop a unique sense of self-reliance, one that's both a blessing and a curse.) Growing up, I often felt like I was shouldering the weight of family expectations alone, (which, in hindsight, was a heavy burden to carry). But as I've grown older, I've come to appreciate the value of those quiet dinners, (where my parents and I would sit together, sharing stories and laughter, and forging a deep bond that's hard to find in other relationships). As I look back on my life, I'm struck by the ways in which being an only child has shaped my approach to life's challenges and relationships. (For instance, I've learned to be more independent and self-sufficient, (which has served me well in my career and personal life).) But I've also come to understand the weight of carrying family expectations alone, (and the importance of setting boundaries and prioritizing my own needs). As I celebrate this milestone birthday, I'm grateful for the lessons I've learned about solitude, independence, and family dynamics, and I'm excited to see how these experiences will continue to shape me in the years to come.
